chapter: Early listening, piano and adolescent conflict
title: Paul Howard's saying and a clear conscience
summary: Paul Howard of Local 767 said if you never lie you never have to remember anything; Thompson reflects on conscience.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: And I believe that and I still believe it, and no matter what happens it seems to be evident I think that the right way is usually the best way. There's a friend of mine here in Los Angeles by the name of Paul Howard. He was the secretary of the black musician's union, the old one, 767, which I was a member when I came to California years ago, and I went over to the integrated union, local 47. But he used to have a saying, that I never forgot. He said, if you never lie you never have to remember anything.
Which I think is a good example of

what I'm talking about. You know, although, you know, we all know that our conscience can bother us. But I think it's very evident today that the conscience won't stop us. You know, if that were the case we wouldn't have so many millionaires, if consciences were that bad, you know, they would kill us.

But the conscience does have something to do with our looks and our personality, and I like to feel that I have at least some normal, happy reactions and pleasant reactions because of the fact I feel that maybe I didn't use some of those tactics that went on.
And you don't have to carry a burden of guilt.
As I said, it's debatable. I think maybe perhaps now that I'm at my age now, I think perhaps I might be able to carry those burdens a little easier. You know?
Well, you'll have to try and find out.
